pages.title: Shop
pages.content:
Shop

Any weave, any tone, any standard size.

Six cloths across the top

The shop opens on the six cloths in one unbroken row, light to dark and light to heavy: Raw Flax, Stonewash, Oat, Moss, Slate, Charcoal. Each tile is the weave itself, and each tile leads to the pieces currently offered in that tone. Raw Flax and Stonewash are plain weave. Oat and Moss are hopsack. Slate and Charcoal are herringbone. All six are 280 cm wide.

The row is the range, not a set of separate collections. A count of results sits with the ordering control, so you can see how many pieces the current sort is showing and rearrange them. The list stays short on purpose. Weave and tone are chosen on the piece, which is why the same six names are not repeated as dozens of separate products.

The pieces and what they cost

Six pieces are on the list, and the price does not change with weave, tone or standard size. A pillowcase pair is €48. A flat sheet is €96. A fitted sheet is €104. A duvet cover is €168. A bed set, the duvet cover with the fitted sheet and the pillowcase pair, is €298. The swatch set, six cloths, is €6, and that €6 is deducted from your first order. Under every name the line is the same: Any weave, any tone.

Adding a piece is a plain underlined link. The pieces are grouped as Sheets, Covers, Pillowcases, Sets and Swatches, and they can be tagged plain, hopsack, herringbone, light or heavy. If the shop catalogue is showing without the cart, the same pieces remain on the page with a short note that the order tools are not running.

Dispatch, delivery and returns

A standard size is dispatched in 3 working days. Made to size is dispatched in 9. Delivery is free over €150. Otherwise it is a flat €9 in the EU and €18 elsewhere. On the road, EU delivery takes 3–5 working days and delivery elsewhere takes 6–10. Returns are accepted for 30 days if the piece is unused. A made-to-size piece cannot be returned.

The counter behind the list is at 14 Ropewalk Lane, Galway, open Tuesday to Saturday, 10:00–17:30. Swatches are the way to feel a tone before a sheet is cut. The header button reads Order swatches, and it leads to the swatch set.

pages.title: Cloths
pages.content:
Cloths

Six washed linens, light to heavy, all 280 cm wide.

Plain weave · 165–170 g/m²

Raw Flax

Raw Flax is the light end of the row. It is a plain weave at 165 g/m², with 5% shrinkage, and the feel is dry and crisp. It is the cloth kept for hot sleepers, and it is the cloth Inés in Porto uses in the journal note The hot sleeper. The width is 280 cm, the same cloth whether the bed is Single, Double, King or a size you send.

It is washed once at 40°C in Galway before it is posted. Beside Stonewash, the other plain weave, Raw Flax is the lighter and drier of the two. The swatch is how you judge that. It gives you the weight, the weave and the hand.

Stonewash

Stonewash is a plain weave at 170 g/m², with 3% shrinkage. It feels soft from day one, which is why it is the cloth for someone buying linen for the first time. It sits second in the row, just heavier than Raw Flax, and it is still a plain weave, not yet the open texture of the hopsacks. The width is 280 cm. It is cut, sewn and washed once at 40°C, then dispatched in 3 working days for a standard size.

There is no breaking-in period written against it. The washed cloth is the cloth you buy. If Raw Flax feels too dry when you hold the two swatches, Stonewash is the neighbouring plain weave, at a difference of 5 g/m² and a softer hand.

Hopsack · 190–195 g/m²

Oat

Oat is a hopsack at 190 g/m², with 3% shrinkage, and the feel is open and textured. It is the cloth named for year-round beds. It is also the cloth Marit in Bergen uses across the journal note Twelve beds, one guest house. The width is 280 cm. In the hand it is looser to the eye than Raw Flax or Stonewash, and lighter than either herringbone.

Guest rooms and ordinary bedrooms both sit inside that year-round line. Like the rest, it is washed once at 40°C before it leaves the workroom. A standard piece in Oat is dispatched in 3 working days. Made to size in Oat adds €24 per piece and takes 9.

Moss

Moss is a hopsack at 195 g/m², with 3% shrinkage, and the feel is even and matte. It is the cloth named for guest rooms. The width is 280 cm. It is the fourth of the six, heavier than Oat by a small step and still a hopsack, not yet the dense face of Slate. The green used for a spec tag elsewhere on the site is taken from this cloth.

That is a mark, not a second product. Moss is cut, sewn and washed once at 40°C in the Galway workroom. For a guest room that needs one calm cloth rather than a contrast of tones, this is the even one. The price of a piece in Moss is the ordinary list, not a guest-house tariff.

Herringbone · 215–225 g/m²

Slate

Slate is a herringbone at 215 g/m², with 3% shrinkage, and the feel is dense and smooth. It is the cloth named for cool rooms. The width is 280 cm. It is the first of the two heavy weaves, darker than Moss and lighter than Charcoal. A slate duvet cover with oat pillowcases appears among the shop's bed photographs. The prices stay the list: duvet cover €168, pillowcase pair €48.

Slate is washed once at 40°C, then folded and tied. Standard dispatch is 3 working days. A sent mattress size is 9, at €24 more per piece.

Charcoal

Charcoal is a herringbone at 225 g/m², the heaviest cloth in the range, with 3% shrinkage. The feel is heavy and draped, and it is the cloth kept for cold sleepers. The width is 280 cm. It closes the row that opened with Raw Flax at 165 g/m². The weight is the point: the cloth hangs, and it covers. That is not offered as a measured warmth, only as the heavy drape at the end of the six.

It is cut and sewn in Galway, washed once at 40°C, and dispatched in 3 working days for Single, Double or King. If you are choosing between Slate and Charcoal, the swatch set is the €6 way to hold 215 g/m² against 225 g/m² before anyone cuts.

The catalogue table

The table at the end repeats the six rows. Columns are Cloth, Weave, g/m², Shrinkage, Feel and Suits. Raw Flax, plain, 165, 5%, dry and crisp, hot sleepers. Stonewash, plain, 170, 3%, soft from day one, first-time linen buyers. Oat, hopsack, 190, 3%, open and textured, year-round beds. Moss, hopsack, 195, 3%, even and matte, guest rooms.

Slate, herringbone, 215, 3%, dense and smooth, cool rooms. Charcoal, herringbone, 225, 3%, heavy and draped, cold sleepers. Every width is 280 cm. Prices are not in this table. They do not change with weave or tone, and they are written in full on Sizes and prices. The home catalogue links here when the short table is not enough.

pages.title: Made to order
pages.content:
Made to order

Four stages, none of them rushed.

Six cloths · €6

Swatch

Swatch is the first stage: feel the six at home. The swatch set is €6, and the €6 is deducted from your first order. Lucía Ferreira looks after swatches and orders. The parcel is cloth, tied with plain cotton tape, without paper labels. Raw Flax, Stonewash, Oat, Moss, Slate and Charcoal travel together so the row can be felt in the room where the bed is, light cloth against heavy cloth.

Nothing is cut at this stage. The set is the same six cloths whether you later choose a standard size or send a mattress size. Ordering the swatches is what the header means by Order swatches. Six swatches, €6, is the whole offer. There is no larger sample pack.

Single, Double, King or your own size

Measure

Measure is the second stage: a standard size, or send your mattress size. Standard is Single, 90×200 cm (35×79 in), Double, 140×200 cm (55×79 in), or King, 180×200 cm (71×79 in). Those three need nothing further from you. For any other mattress, send the size. An email to hello@shikilinen.example is enough, and so is a note brought to 14 Ropewalk Lane, Galway, on Tuesday to Saturday between 10:00 and 17:30.

There is no measuring visit and no form. Write the piece you want, the cloth, and the mattress size in centimetres. Daniel in Leeds ordered on this path. The journal note is A bed that was never standard. His measurements are his own and are not reprinted as a pattern for anyone else.

Cutting from 11:00

Cut and wash

Cut and wash is the third stage. The cloth is cut, sewn, and washed once at 40°C. Tomasz Wrona does the cutting and the making up. Ngozi Adeyemi runs the washroom. Cutting starts from 11:00 on a working day. The Tuesday wash load starts at 09:00, before the shop opens at 10:00. The same wash is used for a standard King and for a size that arrived by email.

Shrinkage stays the catalogue figure: 5% for Raw Flax, 3% for the other five. The workroom does not add a private allowance on top of those numbers. A chalk line on the long table is how the cut is marked. When this stage is finished, the cloth has already had its first wash.

Washed once at 40°C

Post

Post is the fourth stage. The piece is folded, tied and sent. Henrik Aalto runs dispatch. Parcels leave at 16:00. These working-day figures are the workroom, not the time on the road. A standard size is dispatched in 3 working days. A made-to-size piece is dispatched in 9. After that, EU delivery takes 3–5 working days and delivery elsewhere takes 6–10.

Delivery itself is free over €150, a flat €9 in the EU under that, and €18 elsewhere. The cloth you felt as a swatch is the cloth that arrives, washed once, in the tone and weave you named at Measure. No seventh cloth is introduced between the swatch and the parcel.

The made-to-size fee and the lead times

Made to size is + €24 per piece, on top of the list. The list is unchanged: pillowcase pair €48, flat sheet €96, fitted sheet €104, duvet cover €168, bed set €298, swatch set €6. The €24 is per piece, not per order and not per cloth. Weave and tone do not alter it. Lead times stay side by side with the fee. Anything in Single, Double or King is dispatched in 3 working days.

A piece that uses a mattress size you sent is dispatched in 9 working days. The swatch deduction still applies. €6 comes off the first order whether that order is standard or made to size. Currency is the euro.

Can a made-to-size piece be returned?

No. Returns run for 30 days and only for an unused piece in a standard size. A piece cut to a mattress size you sent cannot be returned. The €24 is the charge for that cut. If the size is wrong on the email, correct it before cutting, which starts from 11:00. Write to hello@shikilinen.example while the order is still at Swatch or Measure.

Lucía Ferreira handles the orders. After the cloth is cut, sewn and washed, the return rule has already closed for that piece. A standard piece bought at the same time, if it is unused, can still come back within 30 days. The two rules apply separately when one order mixes both kinds of work.

Six swatches, €6

Start with the cloth in your hands. The €6 is deducted from your first order.

Order swatches

pages.title: Sizes & prices
pages.content:
Sizes & prices

Single, Double and King, in any weave and any tone.

Slate herringbone · 215 g/m²

Single, Double and King

Three sizes are cut without a measuring note. Single is 90×200 cm (35×79 in). Double is 140×200 cm (55×79 in). King is 180×200 cm (71×79 in). The price of a piece is the same for all three. A King duvet cover is €168, and a Single duvet cover is €168. Cloth width behind every size is 280 cm. Anything outside these three rectangles is made to size: send the mattress size, add €24 per piece, and allow 9 working days before dispatch.

The price list

Any weave, any tone, any standard size. Pillowcase pair, €48. Flat sheet, €96. Fitted sheet, €104. Duvet cover, €168. Bed set (duvet cover, fitted sheet, pillowcase pair), €298. Swatch set (six cloths; deducted from your first order), €6. Made to size, per piece, + €24. Raw Flax at 165 g/m² is not cheaper for being lighter. Charcoal at 225 g/m² is not dearer for being heavier.

Plain, hopsack and herringbone share the list. The bed set is its own line at €298, not a discount code.

When is delivery free?

Delivery is free when the order is over €150. A duvet cover at €168 qualifies. A bed set at €298 qualifies. A flat sheet at €96 does not, and a swatch set at €6 does not. Under €150 the charge is a flat €9 in the EU or €18 elsewhere, once per order. After dispatch, EU delivery takes 3–5 working days and delivery elsewhere takes 6–10.

Standard sizes are dispatched in 3 working days. Made to size is dispatched in 9. Those days are the workroom. They are not added again as a second estimate. Returns are 30 days for an unused standard piece. Made-to-size pieces cannot be returned.

pages.title: Care
pages.content:
Care

Wash once, dry in the air, iron if you like.

A wash note for each tone

Raw Flax: 40°C, no softener, plain weave, 165 g/m², dry and crisp, for hot sleepers. Stonewash: 40°C, no softener, plain weave, 170 g/m², soft from day one, for a first linen purchase. Oat: 40°C, no softener, hopsack, 190 g/m², open and textured, for year-round beds. Moss: 40°C, no softener, hopsack, 195 g/m², even and matte, for guest rooms.

Slate: 40°C, no softener, herringbone, 215 g/m², dense and smooth, for cool rooms. Charcoal: 40°C, no softener, herringbone, 225 g/m², heavy and draped, for cold sleepers. Shrinkage stays 5% only for Raw Flax, and 3% for the other five. Width stays 280 cm.

40°C · no softener

Should I wash it before the first night?

The first of the four habits is the wash itself. Every piece has already been washed once at 40°C in the workroom before it is folded, tied and sent. A further wash before the first night is your choice, not a requirement the shop adds. If you do wash it, use 40°C and do not use softener. Ngozi Adeyemi runs the washroom where that first wash happens.

On Tuesday the wash load starts at 09:00, an hour before the shop opens. The same 40°C is used for Raw Flax and for Charcoal. Weight does not change the temperature. Priya Raman's care note on the piece page repeats this and does not add a second temperature for a light cloth or a heavy one.

Drying

Drying is the second habit. In the workroom, wet linen hangs on lines in the washing room, beside a steel sink. That is how the cloth finishes after the single 40°C wash. At home, dry the cloth fully before you put it back on the bed.

All six cloths are treated the same way in the workroom. Shrinkage figures in the catalogue, 5% and 3%, already describe the cloth.

Ironing

Ironing is the third habit, and it is optional. You may iron any of the six, or you may leave the surface the wash gave them. Oat and Moss are open hopsacks. Slate and Charcoal are denser herringbones.

Raw Flax and Stonewash are plain. If you would rather see the cloth as it left Galway, leave it unironed. The piece arrived folded and tied, already washed once. Pressing it is a choice about appearance, not a step the workroom requires before the bed is made.

Softening over time

Softening over time is the fourth habit. Stonewash is soft from day one. Raw Flax starts dry and crisp. Oat is open and textured, Moss even and matte, Slate dense and smooth, Charcoal heavy and draped. Priya Raman's journal note, How a sheet softens, is a care note with no measured claims.

Washing at 40°C without softener is also how the shop avoids coating the yarn. The cloth will be handled, slept on and washed.

Who handles a repair?

Priya Raman handles care advice and repairs. Bring the piece to 14 Ropewalk Lane, Galway, on Tuesday to Saturday, 10:00–17:30, or write to hello@shikilinen.example and mark it for her. The shop will say what it can do before any work starts. A repair is not a new order, and it is not the made-to-size fee of €24.

It is also not a return. Returns remain 30 days, unused, and they exclude made-to-size pieces. A seam that has been in use is a question for Priya, not for the returns rule. Aoife Brennan is on the counter if you would rather hand the piece over in person during those hours.

pages.title: About
pages.content:
About

A shop and a workroom on Ropewalk Lane, since 2014.

Raw Flax to Charcoal

Founded in 2014, narrowed to six

Shiki Linen was founded in 2014 by Aoife Brennan. The shop and the workroom are at 14 Ropewalk Lane, Galway, Ireland. The range was narrowed to six cloths and has stayed on that list. Samir Haddad buys from the mills against those six only. Two are plain weave, Raw Flax and Stonewash. Two are hopsack, Oat and Moss. Two are herringbone, Slate and Charcoal. Weights run from 165 g/m² to 225 g/m².

Every cloth is 280 cm wide. The shop does not keep a seasonal set beside them. A bed outside Single, Double and King is still cut from one of the six, with €24 added per piece. Hot sleepers are pointed to Raw Flax, first-time buyers to Stonewash, year-round beds to Oat, guest rooms to Moss, cool rooms to Slate, and cold sleepers to Charcoal.

Oat hopsack · 190 g/m²

A Tuesday, and the days that follow

The day the brand runs on is a working Tuesday. At 09:00 the wash load starts. At 10:00 the shop opens. Cutting starts from 11:00. Parcels leave at 16:00. The door stays open until 17:30. Wednesday, Thursday, Friday and Saturday use the same shop hours, 10:00–17:30. The counter and the workroom share the address, so a swatch parcel and a King sheet can leave in the same afternoon round.

People buying bedding slowly, hot sleepers, and small guest houses are the ones the hours are kept for. The tone of the place is plain and exact. Nothing on the counter is offered as a health claim, a cure, or a promise of better sleep. The cloth is a weight, a weave and a hand you can check against a swatch.

The seven people

Seven people work here, named in prose rather than set out as a grid of portraits. Aoife Brennan is the owner. She founded the shop in 2014 and works the counter. Tomasz Wrona cuts the cloth and makes the pieces up. Ngozi Adeyemi runs the washroom, including the wash that starts at 09:00 on Tuesday. Lucía Ferreira looks after swatches and orders.

Henrik Aalto runs dispatch, and the parcels go at 16:00. Priya Raman gives care advice and does the repairs. Samir Haddad buys the cloth from the mills. Write to hello@shikilinen.example and the note reaches this room. If you come in person, come between 10:00 and 17:30, Tuesday to Saturday. The wash at 09:00 is before the door opens.

pages.title: Newsletter
pages.content:
Newsletter

A note from the lane when the cloths change.

The notes live on the journal

The four notes are The hot sleeper, Twelve beds, one guest house, A bed that was never standard, and How a sheet softens. They are about Inés and Raw Flax, Marit and Oat, Daniel and a made-to-size bed, and Priya Raman's care note.

Reading them does not change a figure on the list. The swatch set is still €6, deducted from the first order. Delivery is still free over €150. A standard piece is still dispatched in 3 working days, and a made-to-size piece in 9. When a further note exists, it will be a note of the same kind: cloth, an order, or care, written without a health claim.

An order does not start here

If the question is a mattress size, a cloth or a piece, write to hello@shikilinen.example or come to 14 Ropewalk Lane, Galway, Tuesday to Saturday, 10:00–17:30. Lucía Ferreira looks after swatches and orders. Aoife Brennan is on the counter. The shop does not ask you to join a list before it will cut a sheet.

Say which piece you want, which of the six cloths, and either Single, Double, King or the mattress size. Made to size is + €24 per piece and cannot be returned. The journal remains the place to read. The workroom remains the place an order is cut, sewn, washed once at 40°C, folded, tied and sent.

pages.title: Contact
pages.content:
Contact

14 Ropewalk Lane, Galway, Ireland.

Swatch set · €6

Address, email and hours

Shiki Linen is at 14 Ropewalk Lane, Galway, Ireland. The email is hello@shikilinen.example. The shop is open Tuesday to Saturday, 10:00–17:30. Inside the workroom, a Tuesday starts earlier than the door: the wash load at 09:00, the shop open at 10:00, cutting from 11:00, parcels at 16:00.The address, the email and the hours are the route.

Aoife Brennan founded the shop in 2014 and works the counter. A swatch parcel, tied with plain cotton tape, is the photograph beside the address. If you would rather feel the cloths at home, the swatch set is €6, deducted from the first order, and Lucía Ferreira sends it. The hours above are when the door is open. You do not need a separate appointment line to use them.

How do I send a mattress size?

For Single, Double or King, send nothing but the name of the size. Single is 90×200 cm (35×79 in). Double is 140×200 cm (55×79 in). King is 180×200 cm (71×79 in). For any other bed, email the mattress size, or bring it written down to the counter during opening hours. Include the piece: pillowcase pair, flat sheet, fitted sheet, duvet cover or bed set.

Include the cloth if you have already chosen: Raw Flax, Stonewash, Oat, Moss, Slate or Charcoal. Made to size adds €24 per piece, is dispatched in 9 working days, and cannot be returned. Correct a wrong size before cutting starts at 11:00. There is still no form. The email hello@shikilinen.example and the counter at 14 Ropewalk Lane are enough.

Tuesday to Saturday

10:00–17:30 at 14 Ropewalk Lane, Galway. Write to hello@shikilinen.example.

Write to us

posts.title: The hot sleeper
posts.excerpt: Inés, in Porto, chose Raw Flax, the plain 165 g/m² cloth kept for hot sleepers, after feeling all six swatches.
posts.content:
Inés lives in Porto and sleeps hot. She came to Shiki Linen for the cloth the shop names for that, not for a promise about the night. The catalogue has a line for hot sleepers. It does not have a line about curing heat, fixing sleep, or making a room colder. She asked which cloth was the light, dry one. The answer was already printed.

The cloth is Raw Flax. It is a plain weave at 165 g/m², the lightest of the six, with 5% shrinkage. Every other cloth in the range shrinks 3%. The feel is written as dry and crisp. The width is 280 cm, the same width as Stonewash, Oat, Moss, Slate and Charcoal. It can be cut as Single, 90×200 cm (35×79 in), as Double, 140×200 cm (55×79 in), or as King, 180×200 cm (71×79 in). A mattress that matches none of those is made to size. Inés did not need that. She ordered Raw Flax in a standard size, and this note does not turn her order into a pattern for a particular piece or a particular one of the three beds.

She started with the swatches. Six cloths cost €6, and the €6 is deducted from the first order. Lucía Ferreira packs them at 14 Ropewalk Lane and ties the parcel with plain cotton tape. There is no paper label. The cloths have to be told apart by hand, which is the point of sending them. In Porto she kept them in the shop's order, light to heavy, and felt them one against the next.

Stonewash is the other plain weave, 170 g/m², shrinkage 3%, soft from day one, the cloth suggested to someone buying linen for the first time. It was the nearest neighbour to Raw Flax and the easiest one to prefer if softness had been the brief. It was not the brief. Oat, a hopsack at 190 g/m², is open and textured, and it is the cloth named for year-round beds. Moss, a hopsack at 195 g/m², is even and matte, and it is the cloth named for guest rooms. Slate, a herringbone at 215 g/m², is dense and smooth, named for cool rooms. Charcoal, a herringbone at 225 g/m², is heavy and draped, named for cold sleepers. Only Raw Flax carries the words hot sleepers. Inés stopped at the first cloth in the row.

The price did not help her choose, because the price does not move. Any weave, any tone, any standard size: a pillowcase pair is €48, a flat sheet is €96, a fitted sheet is €104, a duvet cover is €168, and a bed set, the duvet cover with the fitted sheet and the pillowcase pair, is €298. Raw Flax costs the same as Charcoal. Light cloth is not a cheaper cloth. The swatch set remained €6, taken off that first order, whether the first order was a pair of pillowcases or a bed set.

What happened next was the ordinary workroom, not a route kept for Porto. Tomasz Wrona cuts and makes up. Cutting starts from 11:00. The cloth is sewn and washed once at 40°C. Ngozi Adeyemi runs the washroom. On Tuesday the wash load starts at 09:00, and the shop opens at 10:00. The finished piece is folded, tied and sent. Henrik Aalto runs dispatch, and parcels leave at 16:00. A standard size is dispatched in 3 working days. Porto takes EU delivery, so the time on the road after that is 3–5 working days. Delivery is free over €150. Under that line, EU delivery is a flat €9. This note does not say which side of €150 her order fell on. Made to size would have added €24 per piece and 9 working days, and that piece could not have been returned. A standard piece, unused, can be returned within 30 days.

The sheet, or whichever piece it was, arrived already washed once. The dry, crisp hand is the hand after that wash. It is not a coating. Priya Raman writes the care notes and does the repairs. Her instruction is the same for every cloth in the six: wash at 40°C, and do not use softener. She does not give a number of washes after which Raw Flax will feel like Stonewash. Her own journal note, How a sheet softens, is a care note with no measured claim. Stonewash is the cloth that is soft on the day it arrives. Raw Flax is the cloth that starts crisp. Inés was not offered a date, a percentage, or a sentence about better sleep.

The shop was founded in 2014 by Aoife Brennan, at 14 Ropewalk Lane, Galway, Ireland. It is open Tuesday to Saturday, 10:00–17:30. Samir Haddad buys the six cloths from the mills, and the counter does not add a seventh because a customer sleeps hot. The answer Inés received is the answer on the cloth page. If you sleep hot, the cloth to feel first is Raw Flax. The way to feel it is the swatch, at home, beside the other five, before anyone in Galway cuts.
